headline: Dry high pressure rules the next 72 hours: sunny, mild Bluegrass afternoons and a gradually weakening Upstate wedge
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Surface high pressure beneath a persistent midlevel ridge keeps Danville and the Bluegrass dry through Tuesday. Sunday and Monday stay mostly sunny with highs near 72°F, while light wind and efficient nighttime cooling support patchy pre-dawn river-valley fog and isolated frost in the coldest sheltered locations. Moisture-starved disturbances bring more mid- and high-level cloud Tuesday without producing rain.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 6:55 AM EDT, KDVK was clear at 39°F with a 37°F dew point, calm wind and visibility above 10 miles. At 6:54 AM, KLEX was 43°F with a 40°F dew point, calm wind, 10-mile visibility and few to scattered clouds from roughly 6,000 to 12,000 feet. No precipitation or official NWS alert was present at issuance.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Danville point. Independent concern is limited to patchy river-valley fog and isolated frost late tonight into Monday morning; a widespread freeze is not expected.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny and mild beneath surface high pressure, with a most likely Danville high near 72°F and light southwest or variable wind. Tonight becomes clear and chilly with a most likely Danville low near 43°F; sheltered valleys may reach the upper 30s with patchy fog or frost toward Monday dawn.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Monday at issuance. Independent concern remains limited to localized river-valley fog or frost late Monday night into Tuesday morning.
days.forecast: Any localized valley fog dissipates during the morning, followed by mostly sunny and mild weather. Danville's most likely high is near 72°F with a light west wind. Monday night remains mostly clear to partly cloudy with a most likely low near 44°F; colder valleys may again see patchy fog or frost toward Tuesday dawn.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Tuesday at issuance, and no significant independent hazard is expected. Localized late-night valley fog remains possible but is less favored if mid- or high-level clouds persist.
days.forecast: Partly cloudy and mild, with periods of mostly cloudy mid- or high-level overcast possible—especially Tuesday afternoon and night—as moisture-starved disturbances pass aloft. Official NWS guidance favors more sunshine, while the full-period GRIB blend favors greater cloud cover; both remain dry. Danville's most likely high is near 72°F with a light easterly wind. Tuesday night has a most likely low near 49°F and only a limited localized valley-fog risk before Wednesday dawn.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky remains dry through Tuesday. Most likely Danville highs are near 72°F each afternoon, with most likely nighttime lows near 43°F, 44°F and 49°F. Patchy pre-dawn river-valley fog and isolated frost remain possible early in the period, but no widespread freeze or official alert is expected.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather and daytime temperatures; moderate-high on nighttime temperatures and moderate on the exact placement of localized valley fog or frost

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: A dry cold-air-damming wedge keeps the Clemson–Central corridor cooler and breezy today; an early stratocumulus deck has already cleared to sunshine. The parent high weakens tonight into Monday, allowing lighter wind and gradual warming. A secondary dry continental air mass arrives Tuesday without producing rain.
upstate.currentConditions: At 6:54 AM EDT, KCEU was clear at 52°F with a 44°F dew point, a northeast wind at 5 kt and 10-mile visibility. At 6:55 AM, KLQK was clear at 49°F with a 44°F dew point, a northeast wind at 4 kt and 10-mile visibility. Earlier Upstate stratus had cleared and was not fog because visibility remained unrestricted. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Clemson point. Independent concern is limited to a breezy northeast wind with gusts around 15–22 mph, remaining below advisory and verification-hazard thresholds. No corridor freeze is expected.
days.forecast: The early stratocumulus has cleared, leaving sunny and cool weather within the dry wedge. Clemson's most likely high is near 69°F. Northeast wind runs 7–12 mph with gusts around 15–22 mph. Tonight turns clear with a most likely Clemson low near 46°F; colder sheltered Central and Pickens County locations may fall near 40°F.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Monday at issuance, and no significant independent hazard is expected. The weekend wedge weakens, with lighter wind and no corridor freeze expected.
days.forecast: The dry wedge weakens, allowing a sunnier and warmer afternoon with a most likely Clemson high near 71°F. East-northeast wind eases to 2–7 mph with gusts around 6–14 mph. Monday night remains mostly clear with a most likely Clemson low near 44°F; sheltered Central and Pickens County locations may reach the upper 30s.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Tuesday at issuance, and no significant independent hazard is expected as a secondary dry continental air mass reinforces the fair-weather pattern.
days.forecast: Sunny and warmer despite a reinforcing dry continental air mass, with a most likely Clemson high near 74°F. Wind remains light from the north or northeast. Tuesday night is mostly clear to partly cloudy with a most likely Clemson low near 48°F and no meaningful corridor fog or freeze signal.

upstate.bottomLine: The Clemson–Central corridor remains dry. Most likely Clemson highs are near 69°F, 71°F and 74°F, with most likely lows near 46°F, 44°F and 48°F. Breezy northeast flow today eases Monday, and no official alert or threshold hazard is expected.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather; moderate-high on temperatures and today's northeast wind, and moderate on the exact pace of wedge erosion Monday

sourceNotes: No official NWS alert was active for the Danville or Clemson point at the 11:13:08Z checks. Official alerts remain separate from this independent analysis.
The 10:42Z Louisville and 10:47Z Greenville-Spartanburg discussions, official point forecasts, current observations and the complete model synthesis agree on a dry 72-hour period.

The locally extracted seven-model package was generated at 11:19:24Z and passed validation with all seven requested models available: 264 files, 9,182 GRIB messages, 237 extracted records and 36 station proposals.

The ECMWF 06Z cycle was attempted, but its +78-hour index was incomplete at the 10:35Z cutoff. The fresh, complete 00Z official cycle was used instead; it was 11.35 hours old at issuance and therefore remained within the 12-hour freshness limit.
HRRR ends at 06Z October 27, RAP at 12Z October 27 and NAM 3-km at 18Z October 27. Their normal partial horizons are disclosed in model status and partial Upstate benchmarks rather than extrapolated.

The exact Tuesday GRIB precipitation window lacks the final 2 hours 21 minutes of this candidate: its last exact QPF interval ends at 09Z October 28, 1 hour 35 minutes before the 10:35Z extraction endpoint and another 46 minutes before candidate validity ends. Every available rate and interval plus all other official, deterministic and ensemble sources show zero meaningful precipitation.

Central Kentucky Tuesday sky cover has a material guidance split: the official NWS point forecast and discussion favor the sunnier outcome, while the validated full-period GRIB blend averages about 70% cloud cover and several deterministic members show extensive mid- or high-level cloud. The forecast therefore allows partly to mostly cloudy periods, especially Tuesday afternoon and night, without implying rain.
NAM and NAM 3-km dense-fog signals were treated as localized valley outliers because current observations, RAP, HRRR, global guidance and official discussions do not support a widespread event.
Upstate NAM and RAP values are explicitly labeled KGSP proxies; NAM 3-km and HRRR are Clemson gridpoint records, with partial later records disclosed. All 31 extracted Upstate GEFS members were dry.

Local BUFKIT 19 KLEX and BUFKIT Warehouse KGSP profiles were reviewed for temperature, inversion, fog, cloud and wind structure. BUFKIT was used as a visualization interface for underlying model cycles, not counted as an additional model.

NWS and College of DuPage radar showed no coherent precipitation near either region. Infrared imagery and fresh observations showed the earlier Upstate stratus had cleared; unrestricted 10-mile visibility confirmed it was not fog.

Chris Bailey's October 25 Kentucky Weather Center post, “Awesome Weather Before November Changes,” supports the dry near-term pattern. Its Halloween and November change is beyond this 72-hour forecast and was excluded.

The latest cumulative accuracy summary was consulted: 29 verified forecast IDs, 78 verified checkpoints and 76.0% all-category accuracy. Updated station corrections, calibrated range widths, regime-specific model weights, fog timing and official-alert handling were applied.

Temperature cards retain calibrated regional coverage widths, while prose supplies narrower most-likely Danville and Clemson point values. Wider overnight ranges represent terrain and station differences rather than uncertainty at one exact point.
